_note: fantasy1-3: the enchanted forest, the valley of giants, the wizard's tower, the costume ball, the castle courtyard and the great hall (Le pays des contes, park sector). Hooks match the paintings; verbs are acted by Monsieur Verbe.

fr_fee_noun.hook: Like the old English word "fay", said FAY: a tiny FÉE (fairy) in a pink petal dress flies over the pond, waving her star-tipped wand.

fr_licorne_noun.hook: "LICK CORN" (lee-KORN): a white LICORNE (unicorn) with a golden spiral horn LICKS a big yellow ear of CORN set on a tree stump.

fr_sirene_noun.hook: Plain: like "siren", said see-REHN: a red-haired SIRÈNE (mermaid) with a green fish tail sits on a mossy rock in the forest pond, singing.

fr_centaure_noun.hook: Plain: like "centaur", said sahn-TOR: a young CENTAURE, half boy and half chestnut horse, leaps across the clearing carrying a basket of red apples.

fr_elfe_noun.hook: Plain: like "elf", said ELF: a slim ELFE with pointed ears sits high in the tree and plays a wooden flute.

fr_farfadet_noun.hook: "FARFA(lle) DAY" (far-fah-DEH): a tiny green FARFADET (sprite) wearing a big yellow FARFALLE pasta bow as his bow tie swings on a bluebell on a sunny DAY.

fr_gnome_noun.hook: Plain: like "gnome" with the g sounded, said GNOHM: a GNOME in a tall red pointed hat pushes a wheelbarrow full of mushrooms.

fr_lutin_noun.hook: "LUTE TAN" (lew-TAN): a cheeky red LUTIN (imp) in sunglasses works on his sunTAN on top of a red toadstool, strumming a LUTE.

fr_nain_noun.hook: "NAN": a bearded NAIN (dwarf) with a lantern happily bites into a big round NAAN bread.
fr_nain_noun.note: Said about a person with dwarfism it can be hurtful; 'personne de petite taille' is the respectful term.

fr_phenix_noun.hook: Plain: like "phoenix", said fay-NEEKS: a red-and-gold PHÉNIX with a long flowing tail glides across the sky.

fr_griffon_noun.hook: Plain: like "griffin", said gree-FOHN: a GRIFFON, eagle head and wings on a lion's body, rests proudly on a high rocky crag.

fr_geant_noun.hook: "JAY ON!" (zhay-AHN): a blue JAY perches ON the thumb of a kindly GÉANT (giant) sitting on a boulder.

fr_troll_noun.hook: Plain: like "troll", said TROLL: a mossy green TROLL stands waist-deep in the stream beside the stone footbridge and waves hello.

fr_ogre_noun.hook: Plain: like "ogre", said OGR: a friendly OGRE with small tusks sits on a log and reads a picture book to three little mice.

fr_dragon_noun.hook: Plain: like "dragon", said drah-GOHN: a friendly green DRAGON wearing a daisy chain sleeps smiling on the grass.

fr_sorciere_noun.hook: Like "sorceress" with the end cut off, said sor-SYEHR: a friendly SORCIÈRE (witch) in a tall pointed purple hat sweeps the tower floor with her straw broom while her black cat trots beside the broom.

fr_potion_noun.hook: Plain: like "potion", said po-SYOHN: a bubbling pink POTION fizzes with heart-shaped bubbles in a round glass flask on the little table by the window.

fr_sortilege_noun.hook: "SORT TEA LEDGE" (sor-tee-LEZH): a swirl of golden SORTILÈGE (spell) sparkles rising from the enchanter's tuba SORTS the TEAcups by colour onto a high LEDGE.

fr_grimoire_noun.hook: "GRIN, MWAH!" (gree-MWAHR): a fat old GRIMOIRE (spell book) on a lectern has a friendly face on its cover; it GRINS and blows a kiss, "MWAH!"

fr_magicien_noun.hook: Like English 'magician', said mah-zhee-SYAN: a visiting MAGICIEN (magician) in a black top hat and cape holds up a white rabbit, his top hat on his head.

fr_chaudron_noun.hook: "CHAUD (hot) + DRONE" (shoh-DROHN): a little toy DRONE hovers over a big black CHAUDRON (cauldron) that bubbles HOT on the fire.

fr_sorcier_noun.hook: Like English 'sorcerer', said sor-SYAY: an old SORCIER (wizard) with a long white beard and a starry blue robe throws both arms up and cheers "YAY!" beside his bubbling cauldron.

fr_enchanteur_noun.hook: Like English 'enchanter', said ahn-shahn-TUHR: an ENCHANTEUR (enchanter) in a green velvet robe plays a shiny TUBA, and golden sparkles pour out of its bell.

fr_momie_noun.hook: "MOMMY" (mo-MEE): a little girl dressed as a MOMIE (mummy), loosely wrapped in white bandages, hugs her MOMMY, who kneels to hug her back.

fr_vampire_noun.hook: Like English 'vampire', said vahn-PIER: a child in a VAMPIRE cape with a high collar peers out of the window of a short cardboard VAN.

fr_fantome_noun.hook: Like English 'phantom', said fahn-TOHM: a child in a white sheet FANTÔME (ghost) costume cools off with a paper FAN while reading a big TOME.

fr_orc_noun.hook: Plain: like "orc", said ORK: a child in an ORC costume with green face paint and soft foam tusks flexes his arms like a strongman. Not orque (la), the orca.

fr_loup_garou_noun.hook: "LOUP (wolf) + kanGAROO" (loo-gah-ROO): a boy in a fluffy LOUP-GAROU (werewolf) costume with pointy wolf ears hops across the dance floor like a kanGAROO, both feet in the air.

fr_gobelin_noun.hook: Plain: like "goblin", said gob-LAN: a boy in a green GOBELIN (goblin) costume with big pointy ears is about to GOBBLE the slice of party cake on his plate.

fr_monstre_noun.hook: Like English 'monster', said MOHNSTR: a child in a fluffy purple MONSTRE (monster) costume with big googly eyes dances to the music.

fr_douer_verb.hook: "DUET" (DWAY): Monsieur Verbe in a red beret kneels by the royal cradle and hands the baby twins a tiny golden harp; he ENDOWS them with a gift, and at once they sing a DUET together.
fr_douer_verb.why: fantasy3; Monsieur Verbe (red beret); say from vocab
ex: La fée a doué les jumeaux d'une belle voix.
The fairy endowed the twins with a beautiful voice.

fr_redevenir_verb.hook: "RUDDY VENEER" (ruh-duh-vuh-NEER): Monsieur Verbe in a gold beret brushes a fresh RUDDY VENEER onto a battered old treasure chest; the half he has done shines like new, so the chest BECOMES beautiful AGAIN.
fr_redevenir_verb.why: fantasy3; Monsieur Verbe (gold beret); say from vocab

fr_materialiser_verb.hook: Like English "materialize", said mah-tay-ryah-lee-ZAY: Monsieur Verbe in a red beret sweeps his gloved hands apart and a big round pie MATERIALIZES on the picnic table in a puff of sparkles.
fr_materialiser_verb.why: fantasy3; Monsieur Verbe (red beret); say from vocab
ex: D'un geste, le mime matérialise une tarte sur la table.
With one gesture, the mime materializes a pie on the table.

fr_tromper_verb.hook: "TRUMPET" (trohn-PAY): Monsieur Verbe in a red beret DECEIVES the castle herald: he puffs into a long golden TRUMPET and, instead of a fanfare, a paper party streamer shoots out at the startled herald.
fr_tromper_verb.why: fantasy3; Monsieur Verbe (red beret); say from vocab
ex: Avec sa fausse trompette, le mime trompe le héraut.
With his trick trumpet, the mime deceives the herald.

fr_trahir_verb.hook: "TRAY, HEAR" (trah-EER): Monsieur Verbe in a green beret balances a silver TRAY and leans in to HEAR the princess whisper her secret to her friend; a carrier pigeon already waits on his tray to fly off with it: he BETRAYS her.
fr_trahir_verb.why: fantasy3; Monsieur Verbe (green beret); say from vocab

fr_predire_verb.hook: Like English "predict", said pray-DEER: Monsieur Verbe in a gold beret gazes into a crystal ball that shows a little grey rain cloud; he PREDICTS rain and already holds an open umbrella over a curious young queen.
fr_predire_verb.why: fantasy3; Monsieur Verbe (gold beret); say from vocab

fr_venger_verb.hook: Like English "avenge", said vahn-ZHAY: a goose by the fountain splashed Monsieur Verbe's red beret, so he takes his REVENGE, sprinkling the goose with his watering can while it flaps and honks.
fr_venger_verb.why: fantasy3; Monsieur Verbe (red beret); say from vocab
ex: Le mime veut venger son chapeau mouillé.
The mime wants to avenge his wet hat.

fr_destiner_verb.hook: Like English "destiny", said days-tee-NAY: Monsieur Verbe in a red beret kneels and offers a glass slipper on a velvet cushion to the girl it was DESTINED for, and it fits her foot.
fr_destiner_verb.why: fantasy3; Monsieur Verbe (red beret); say from vocab
ex: Cette pantoufle de verre lui était destinée.
This glass slipper was destined for her.

fr_maudire_verb.hook: "MOW, DEER!" (moh-DEER): Monsieur Verbe in a gold beret stops MOWING the castle lawn to CURSE the DEER munching his rose bush, shaking his fist while it chews on calmly.
fr_maudire_verb.why: fantasy3; Monsieur Verbe (gold beret); say from vocab
ex: Le jardinier maudit le cerf qui mange ses roses.
The gardener curses the deer that eats his roses.

fr_enchanter_verb.hook: Like English "enchant", said ahn-shahn-TAY: Monsieur Verbe in a red beret winds a golden music box, and its tiny dancer ENCHANTS a family of hedgehogs, who sit spellbound.
fr_enchanter_verb.why: fantasy3; Monsieur Verbe (red beret); say from vocab
ex: La boîte à musique enchante les hérissons.
The music box enchants the hedgehogs.

fr_pressentir_verb.hook: "PRESENT EAR" (pray-sahn-TEER): Monsieur Verbe in a gold beret holds a wrapped PRESENT to his EAR, eyes closed, and already SENSES what is inside before he opens it.
fr_pressentir_verb.why: fantasy3; Monsieur Verbe (gold beret); say from vocab

fr_pervertir_verb.hook: "PEAR FUR" (pehr-vehr-TEER): Monsieur Verbe in a green beret sprinkles mischief dust on a golden PEAR in the fruit bowl, and it grows green FUR and goes bad: he SPOILS it.
fr_pervertir_verb.why: fantasy3; Monsieur Verbe (green beret); say from vocab
fr_pervertir_verb.note: Formal. Mostly « corrompre » in everyday speech; the related adjective « pervers » is strongly negative.

fr_advenir_verb.hook: Like the start of English "adventure", said ahd-vuh-NEER: Monsieur Verbe in a gold beret kneels by the fireplace and opens a huge storybook, and a little sailing ship sails out of its pages on a painted blue wave: an ADVENTURE HAPPENS.
fr_advenir_verb.why: fantasy3; Monsieur Verbe (gold beret); say from vocab

fr_entrevoir_verb.hook: "ENTER... VOILÀ!" (ahn-truh-VWAHR): Monsieur Verbe in a gold beret draws back the heavy red curtain and peeks into the dim alcove, where he MAKES OUT a white peacock fanning its tail.
fr_entrevoir_verb.why: fantasy3; Monsieur Verbe (gold beret); say from vocab
ex: Par la fente du rideau, j'entrevois un paon.
Through the gap in the curtain, I make out a peacock.

fr_hanter_verb.hook: "AUNTIE" (ahn-TAY): Monsieur Verbe in a red beret drapes a lace tablecloth over his head like a ghost and HAUNTS his old AUNTIE's armchair, waving and wailing "oooh" beside her while she knits and smiles.
fr_hanter_verb.why: fantasy3; Monsieur Verbe (red beret); say from vocab

fr_ruser_verb.hook: "A RUSE, EH?" (rew-ZAY): Monsieur Verbe in a red beret wears joke glasses with a fake nose and moustache and tiptoes past the sleeping castle dog to reach the cookie jar: he USES his CUNNING.
fr_ruser_verb.why: fantasy3; Monsieur Verbe (red beret); say from vocab
ex: Le mime ruse pour prendre un biscuit.
The mime uses cunning to take a cookie.

fr_invoquer_verb.hook: Like English "invoke", said an-voh-KAY: Monsieur Verbe in a red beret raises both arms at the tall open window and INVOKES the North Wind; a puffy cloud with a cheeky face blows in and lifts his scarf.
fr_invoquer_verb.why: fantasy3; Monsieur Verbe (red beret); say from vocab
ex: Le mime invoque le vent du nord.
The mime calls up the north wind.
